newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait share index hits peak, volume edges down.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait share index hits peak, volume edges down.

text.p: For the third consecutive week year-end profits by listed firms pushed the share index to a record high, market analysts said on Thursday.
"Dealers are slowing down due to Ramadan (Moslem fasting month). But the index shows the impact of good company results," said an analyst.
The index rose 30.9 points to 2,054.9 points in the week to Wednesday with gainers leading losers 28-15 and 14 non-movers, figures released by the Kuwait Stock Exchange on Thursday show.

The daily average for value of traded shares fell to 37.2 million dinars ($123.2 million) during the week to Wednesday from 40.2 million. Volume fell to a daily average of 128.3 million shares from 134.4 million.
Trading is expected to be more active in the weeks after the Eid al-Fitr holiday next week, which marks the end of the fasting month, an analyst said.
Investment firms were the most active sector in terms of traded value with 67.1 million dinars, followed by banks with 32 million and property firms with 28.8.
Commercial Bank, Gulf Bank, Securities Group, Coast Development, United Realty National Industries and Livestock Trade & Transport.
Only nationals of Gulf Arab states -- Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Kuwait -- can trade on the exchange. Foreign residents can invest in mutual funds.
